doc.title: Kent Jordan interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 22, 2006

chapter: The music business and jazz education
title: The Out of this World release
summary: The album with Elton Herron's arrangement, produced with Orrin Keepnews, and choosing recording moments carefully.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Before we actually started we were talking a little bit about how marketing is changing, has changed and will continue to change. You had a release that kind of sat around for a while, “Out of this World”?

I’ll have to get that to you, I’m sorry I didn’t bring any of that music with me because I was really just concentrating on what I had to do here. Yeah I did it and it was a really, I think probably like some of the best playing in terms of what I wanted to convey. And obviously we did “Out of this World” that was influenced by John Coltrane. It’s not his composition but we — I say we — but Elton Herron who is a great colleague and a friend and a relative, arranged it for me and it’s just one of those things, one of those sessions, Orrin Keepnews helped me produce it and it was just one of those things that I felt like © Fillius Jazz Archive -17-

after the tape started rolling I gave everything I could give at that moment. And then I had to go on to something else. And with the recording industry changing now you really sort of have to pick your moments when you want to go in and do something that’s of value versus let me go into the studio and do a CD because I don’t want people to forget about me. I don’t really operate like that. You know, just come up with some tunes. For me it’s kind of a process and then when I’m there I’ll go yes, let’s go in and do something.
